name: serverexternalpackages-not-enough-nextjs-15-webpack
hook: serverExternalPackages does not prevent webpack from analyzing undici/@napi-rs/canvas internals
body: In Next.js 15.5.9, serverExternalPackages prevents packages from being included in the serverless function bundle, but webpack still analyzes the package code when processing imports from client-side code or other packages. This analysis encounters node: imports (node:console, node:dns, etc.) inside undici, causing UnhandledSchemeError. The fix is to add these packages to webpackConfig.externals for non-client builds (server + edge), which prevents webpack from analyzing their internals entirely.
why: webpackConfig.externals and serverExternalPackages serve complementary roles — serverExternalPackages handles the serverless deployment bundling, while webpackConfig.externals prevents webpack's static analysis from processing the package. Both are needed for server-only packages that contain node: imports.

name: webpack-externals-must-be-conditional-isclient
hook: webpackConfig.externals must only be added for non-client builds using !isClient guard
body: When adding packages to webpackConfig.externals, you MUST use the isClient parameter (second arg to webpack callback) to only add externals for non-client builds. Adding externals unconditionally (or only for server builds using webpackConfig.name checks) can cause the package to be treated as external in ALL webpack builds including client, which breaks the client build because webpack can't find the module at runtime. Use `if (!isClient) { webpackConfig.externals.push(...) }`.
why: Next.js 15.5.9's webpack callback receives isClient as a boolean flag. When isClient is true (client build), the externals should NOT be added because the package must be bundled for the browser. When isClient is false or undefined (server/edge), externals should be added because the package is loaded from node_modules at runtime.

name: empty-stub-file-needed-for-node-native-alias
hook: webpack resolve.alias for .node$ files requires an actual file to redirect to
body: When using webpackConfig.resolve.alias to redirect .node native binary files to a stub, webpack requires the stub path to be an actual file that exists on disk. The empty stub file must be a real .js file (not .ts since webpack resolves .js extensions). Create src/server/utils/empty-stub.js with an empty export.
why: webpack's resolve.alias uses the standard webpack resolve algorithm, which requires the target of an alias to exist as a resolvable file. A non-existent path causes webpack to fail with 'cannot find module'.
